analysis_mode: authorized static only; no firmware execution/device operations

findings.summary: Startup loads list and exclusions, refreshes existing PIDs (not starts), normally stops prior tracked processes with mode 1, then starts enabled records. SUPERVISION.md startup call-site description at 0x1467e was inaccurate.
limits: Observed startup configuration is not proof every possible writer/child is supervised.

findings.summary: Three parser iterations per line. Comma-delimited prefixes can be empty; final remainder with no comma is accepted only at length >3. Matching is std::string::find against process name; whitespace is not trimmed on this path. Empty prefix can match all names.
limits: C++ allocation/stream internals intentionally not reconstructed.

findings.summary: Each record enabled byte +0x18 is first set to 1, a match sets 0; signed positive tracked PID at +0 causes kill(pid,9). PID then becomes -1 regardless of kill result. No wait, MCU command or descendant traversal occurs in this function.
limits: No map flush/close acknowledgment; disabling supervisor restart is not a write barrier.

findings.summary: Reload marks all records enabled first, so records with no matching parsed token become re-enabled. Open-failure branch also enables all. Event 8 directly reloads without reset; event 9 is not the only re-enable mechanism. Reload itself never starts records. Missing non-key records can be started by a later periodic scan, while missing key records take status-2 recovery/escalation.
limits: Non-destructive re-enable of flags exists statically, but no validated controlled all-writer restart interface or safe operational sequence is established.
No proposed exclusion payload or robot operation is supplied.

findings.summary: IPC 0x07030342 writes exclusions first, then uses strlen on payload: unsigned length >2 -> event 8, <=2 -> event 9. Embedded NUL affects effective length; packet length is not used for selection. File write failure cannot block queued event.
limits: RecvPacket terminator/bounds guarantees remain unresolved; this is not a claim that all malformed packets behave predictably.

findings.summary: Event 9 invokes kill commands for three network clients, then WdogResetConfigFiles, then falls through event-8 reload. Reset helper deletes Wi-Fi/device/config paths, upload flag, exclusions and endpoint files and executes recursive rriot deletion. Bounded side-effect analysis only.
limits: Root path base is a runtime-populated BSS buffer at 0x34b64; exact original object layout is unknown.
No credentials or captured device configuration content included. Return values of deletion calls are not checked.

findings.summary: After reload returns, dispatcher calls WdogSendIpcPacket(0x03070343,NULL,0). r10 is assembled from 0x0343/0x0307 before the loop, then loaded into r0. SUPERVISION.md statement that no reply was found must be narrowed: an acknowledgment-like outbound send exists.
limits: SendPacket result only logged; delivery/correlation not proven. This call cannot confirm killed writers exited or flushed. Event 9 also reaches this send by fallthrough.

findings.summary: Internal SysV queue uses key 0x80001000, type 1, four-byte event; msgsnd is nonblocking (0x800). Sender returns send-success boolean but IPC loop ignores it. Blocking reader retries errno 4. Queue delivery/completion is not a writer barrier.

Normal stop first signals tracked PID using helper; mode 1 calls heartbeat control 120 then bounded proc-status polling for each positive PID, mode 2 does so only for rrlogd, mode 0 does not. Failed/no wait falls back to SIGKILL. After sleep(1), positive tracked PIDs are probed with kill(pid,0); return 1 if any probe succeeds, else 0. SUPERVISION.md heartbeat statement was overbroad.
limits: Successful wait clears tracked PID. No waitpid/fsync/child-tree accounting; ignored kill errors and PID reuse limit completion evidence.

findings.summary: Mode-0 signal helper parses State:/PPid: in /proc/<pid>/status: zombie Z -> kill(parent,9); otherwise kill(pid,1), NOT SIGTERM. Wait helper merely polls fopen(status), sleeps one second, counts down attempts; any open failure is success-like. Missing status/negative PID in signal helper is also success-like.
limits: No proof of graceful shutdown or child exit. String bytes State:/PPid: additionally match binary file offsets 0x1084c/0x10854 (mapped read-only VAs 0x2084c/0x20854).

findings.summary: Init opens /dev/watchdog, asks timeout 16 (0xc0045706), applies HWDOG_OPTION/default 1 through vendor ioctl 0xc004570b, then option 2 through 0x80045704. Feed-once invokes ioctl 0x80045705 with literal third arg 1 and increments counter even on failure. Close writes V byte 0x56 then closes fd. Stop-feeder cancels and joins only watchdog thread before close.
limits: Kernel/vendor driver semantics, option behavior, magic-close acceptance and reset safety are unproven. Feed counter is not accepted-feed evidence. No map-writer synchronization.

findings.summary: Registered signal set: 15,2,3,11,7,10,12,4,5,6,8,1. Every handled signal refreshes/checks PIDs and closes watchdog first; 10/12 stop mode 0/1 respectively, disable MCU heartbeat, mark supervisor stopped and return. Other signals enter stop/teardown/exit, with signal 11 early-return guard after common prelude. Signal 15 also disables MCU heartbeat.
limits: SIGHUP is not reload-only. No async-signal safety or hardware/MCU reset safety claim.

findings.summary: Surviving symbols retained; corrected ABI return to int after checking r0=r6 epilogue. value 0 becomes 60; other bits preserved. Sends (0xd3,4,&value,1), at most three attempts with 20ms sleeps after failure. Locally initializes/closes UART only if needed. disable wrapper passes -1 (ff ff ff ff).
limits: Only command encoding and userspace return/retry paths confirmed. Meaning of values, MCU acknowledgment semantics and normal heartbeat producer remain unresolved.

findings.summary: Launcher at true entry 0x1ac08 passes Thumb target 0x1af19 to pthread_create. Even candidate entry 0x1af18 has bytes 38b503f00dfc. Baseline has neither instructions nor any function for 0x1af18..0x1af69. Parent approved read-only discovery and explicit gap; no function/disassembly created.
findings.prior_trace: analysis/storage-traces.txt:453-462 documents feed/init and eight-second loop; not represented as generated C because baseline contains only bytes at that range.
findings.proposed_parent_recovery: Separate reviewed tooling/baseline recovery: decode Thumb candidate 0x1af18, confirm body through return at 0x1af68 and create only that verified entry; requires a parent decision and replayable recovery support, not lane schema-v1 guessing.
limits: No named/typed C for absent thread body; named launcher/one-shot feeder/init/close/stop are delivered.
Candidate entry is not silently treated as a known Ghidra function.

findings.summary: Normal MCU heartbeat producer and command-0xd3 implementation are not recovered. Rootfs firmware/img contains multiple opaque model-specific MCU blobs; none was selected/analyzed as authoritative MCU implementation. Inspected rootfs boot/usr/src and module filenames did not expose watchdog driver implementation. No device state or reset safety follows from userspace code.
limits: Presence of opaque MCU update blobs is not absence of firmware, and is not proof which image runs.
No kernel watchdog source/implementation was verified; absence from inspected rootfs paths does not prove absence on device.

corrections_to_prior_prose.correct: 0x1467e refreshes PIDs; normal stop is 0x146a8; enabled-process start is 0x146d0.

corrections_to_prior_prose.old: How to re-enable without event 9 is unknown; no completion reply found.
corrections_to_prior_prose.correct: Event 8 non-destructively resets enabled flags before matching; open failure also enables all. Outbound zero-payload 0x03070343 is sent after reload, but does not prove delivery/correlation/quiescence or a controlled all-writer restart.

corrections_to_prior_prose.old: When normal stop runs it sends heartbeat-control value 120.
corrections_to_prior_prose.correct: Only mode 1, and mode 2 for rrlogd, send 120; mode 0 does not. First signal helper uses SIGHUP for non-zombie and SIGKILL to parsed parent for zombie.
C strlen, not packet-length field, selects >2 event 8 versus <=2 event 9; write occurs first and has no status to caller.

read_only_startup_configuration.finding: Static configured sysinit rcS, respawn WatchDoge. Actual runtime init status not measured.
run_scripts invokes executable init scripts synchronously through shell pipeline.
Reserve startup script is backgrounded; no writer-start ordering barrier.
Configured rr_loader and RoboController key=1, AppProxy key=0; commands use setsid/background. This is not a complete descendant/writer inventory.
Read-only inspection confirms separate background application outside normal supervisor list; private environment/config contents not reproduced.

type_interpretation.WdogStopMode: Owned Wdog enum, ABI size 4; no original C++ layouts or other-lane type copies proposed.

open_questions: Can parent recover the independently referenced absent feeder function in a replayable approved way?
Which process sends normal MCU heartbeat, and which MCU blob/handler is active?
What do vendor watchdog option and V close do in the actual kernel configuration?
How can all map writers and descendants be stopped/drained/restarted without invoking key-process recovery, reset or stale-cache loading?
Does acknowledgment-like message 0x03070343 have request correlation/delivery semantics at its recipient?
nonclaims: Static exports/data checks do not prove robot runtime behavior.
No safe restore instructions, payload recipes, IPC sends, signals, shell commands for the robot or device operations performed.
